articles/bindings.html.title: Data Bindings | CodeUI Documentation
articles/bindings.html.keywords: Data Bindings Unity UI Toolkit supports Data Binding to automatically synchronize model properties with UI controls. CodeUI provides type-safe lambda expression extensions that eliminate string-based property path errors. 1. The Problem with String-Based Bindings Traditional UI Toolkit bindings rely on magic strings to reference property names on data sources: // Error-prone: Hardcoded string property paths label.SetBinding("text", new DataBinding { dataSourcePath = new PropertyPath("PlayerName"), bindingMode = BindingMode.ToTarget }); Why String-Based Bindings Are Problematic No Compile-Time Verification: A typo in "PlayerName" (such as "Playername" or "Player_Name") compiles without warnings and fails silently at runtime. Refactoring Vulnerability: Renaming properties in your ViewModel or ScriptableObject breaks string paths across your project without triggering IDE refactoring tools. No Type Safety: The compiler cannot verify whether the source property type matches the target UI element property type. 2. Strongly-Typed Lambda Bindings in CodeUI CodeUI replaces string paths with C# Expression Lambdas (Expression<Func<TData, TValue>>). The compiler extracts property names directly from code expressions, providing full compile-time safety and automatic refactoring support. Text Binding (BindText) Use BindText to bind the text of any TextElement (e.g., Label, Button) to a string property: // Strongly-typed string binding label.BindText(playerData, data => data.PlayerName); Value Binding (BindValue) Use BindValue for interactive controls implementing INotifyValueChanged<TValue> (e.g., Toggle, Slider, TextField, IntegerField): // Two-way binding for interactive controls toggle.BindValue(settingsData, s => s.MuteAudio); slider.BindValue(playerData, p => p.VolumeLevel); By default, BindValue uses BindingMode.TwoWay, meaning user edits in the UI update the data source immediately, and model changes update the UI. 3. General Property Binding (SetUnityBinding) For custom properties or non-standard bindings, use SetUnityBinding with target and source lambda expressions: // Bind custom property (e.g., progress bar value) progressBar.SetUnityBinding( targetProperty: bar => bar.value, dataSource: playerData, applyDataSource: true, sourceProperty: data => data.HealthRatio, mode: BindingMode.ToTarget ); 4. Assigning Data Sources (SetUnityDataSource) Data sources can be assigned directly to individual elements or to a root container: // Set data source on root container root.SetUnityDataSource(viewModel);

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | CodeUI Documentation
articles/getting-started.html.keywords: Getting Started CodeUI provides a fluent C# interface for constructing Unity UI Toolkit components. 1. Creating Components with BaseUI Attach a UIDocument component to a GameObject and inherit from BaseUI to construct your interface inside Generate: using CodeUI; using CodeUI.Extensions; using CodeUI.Tokens; using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.UIElements; public class SettingsScreen : BaseUI { protected override void Generate(VisualElement root) { root.Column() .Padding(Spacing.MD) .WithChildren( new Label("Settings").FontSize(FontSize.LG), new Toggle("Mute Audio") .OnValueChanged<Toggle, bool>(evt => AudioListener.pause = evt.newValue), Spacer.Vertical(Spacing.MD), new Button(() => RebuildUI()) .SetText("Refresh") ); } } 2. Layout & Positioning CodeUI provides shorthand extension methods for standard Flexbox properties: Method Description Row() Sets flex direction to horizontal (FlexDirection.Row) Column() Sets flex direction to vertical (FlexDirection.Column) Center() Centers elements horizontally and vertically (Align.Center, Justify.Center) Absolute() Sets position mode to absolute (Position.Absolute) Relative() Sets position mode to relative (Position.Relative) 3. Styling & Tokens Standard design tokens ensure consistent spacing, typography, and layout boundaries across components: Spacing: Spacing.XS (4px), Spacing.SM (8px), Spacing.MD (16px), Spacing.LG (24px), Spacing.XL (32px), Spacing.XXL (48px) FontSize: FontSize.XS (12px), FontSize.SM (14px), FontSize.MD (16px), FontSize.LG (20px), FontSize.XL (28px), FontSize.XXL (40px) Radius: Radius.None (0px), Radius.SM (4px), Radius.MD (8px), Radius.LG (16px), Radius.Full (999px) 4. Event Handling Events can be attached directly to visual elements during instantiation: button.OnClick(() => Debug.Log("Button clicked")) .OnHover(isHovering => button.ToggleClasses(isHovering, "hovered")); 5. Animations & Transitions Smooth CSS transitions can be defined using the type-safe TransitionProperty enum: card.Transition(TransitionProperty.scale, durationSeconds: 0.2f, EasingMode.EaseOutCubic) .OnHover(hovered => card.Scale(hovered ? 1.05f : 1.0f));

index.html.title: CodeUI Documentation | CodeUI Documentation
index.html.keywords: CodeUI Documentation CodeUI is a fluent, declarative C# framework for building user interfaces with Unity UI Toolkit (UIElements). It removes the boilerplate associated with UXML and USS by enabling full layout, styling, event binding, and state transitions directly in code. Features Fluent API: Chain extension methods to style, layout, and position visual elements directly in C#. Design Tokens: Standardized constants for spacing (Spacing), font sizes (FontSize), and corner radii (Radius). Unity Data Binding: Declarative wrappers for binding properties to Unity Data Sources via BindText and BindValue. Type-Safe Transitions: Animate CSS properties cleanly using the TransitionProperty enum. Zero External Dependencies: Built natively on top of UnityEngine.UIElements. Quick Example Inherit from BaseUI to define your component hierarchy: using CodeUI; using CodeUI.Extensions; using CodeUI.Tokens; using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.UIElements; public class MainMenuUI : BaseUI { protected override void Generate(VisualElement root) { root.Column() .Center() .Padding(Spacing.LG) .WithChildren( new Label("Main Menu") .FontSize(FontSize.XL) .Margin(bottom: Spacing.MD), new Button(() => Debug.Log("Start Game")) .SetText("Play") .Padding(Spacing.SM, Spacing.MD) .BorderRadius(Radius.MD) ); } } Documentation Getting Started Guide API Reference
